title: The Signing of the Declaration of Independence
headline: INDEPENDENCE DECLARED: Fifty-Six Men Put Their Names to Treason and Changed the World Forever
summary: On July 4, 1776, delegates to the Continental Congress formally adopted the Declaration of Independence, severing ties with Britain and launching a radical experiment in self-governance.

title: The Boston Tea Party
headline: TEA DUMPED IN HARBOR: Colonists Destroy 342 Chests of British Tea in Midnight Protest
summary: On December 16, 1773, American colonists disguised as Mohawk Indians boarded three ships and dumped 342 chests of tea into Boston Harbor, igniting a chain of events that led to revolution.

title: The Storming of the Bastille
headline: BASTILLE FALLS: Paris Mob Storms Royal Fortress as French Revolution Erupts
summary: On July 14, 1789, a crowd of Parisians stormed the Bastille fortress, a symbol of royal authority, marking the beginning of the French Revolution and the end of absolute monarchy in France.

title: The Trail of Tears
headline: FORCED MARCH: Thousands of Cherokee Die on 1,000-Mile Journey West
summary: In 1838, the U.S. government forcibly removed approximately 16,000 Cherokee from their ancestral homeland. Roughly 4,000 died on the brutal march westward known as the Trail of Tears.

title: The California Gold Rush
headline: GOLD DISCOVERED: Hundreds of Thousands Race to California in History's Greatest Treasure Hunt
summary: After James Marshall found gold at Sutter's Mill in January 1848, some 300,000 people flooded into California, transforming a remote territory into a state and reshaping American westward expansion.

title: The Opening of the Suez Canal
headline: EAST MEETS WEST: Suez Canal Opens, Slashing Voyage from Europe to Asia by Thousands of Miles
summary: On November 17, 1869, the Suez Canal opened after ten years of construction, connecting the Mediterranean Sea to the Red Sea and revolutionizing global trade and naval strategy.

title: The Invention of Photography
headline: REALITY CAPTURED: Daguerre Unveils Process That Freezes Time in Silver and Light
summary: In 1839, Louis Daguerre publicly demonstrated the daguerreotype process, giving humanity the power to capture and preserve exact images of the world for the first time.

title: Britain Abolishes the Slave Trade
headline: SLAVE TRADE ABOLISHED: Parliament Votes to End Centuries of Human Trafficking Across the Atlantic
summary: On March 25, 1807, the British Parliament passed the Slave Trade Act, making it illegal to buy or sell enslaved people throughout the British Empire after decades of abolitionist campaigning.

title: The Irish Home Rule Crisis
headline: IRELAND ON THE BRINK: Home Rule Bill Passes but Ulster Volunteers Threaten Civil War
summary: The Third Home Rule Bill of 1914 promised self-governance to Ireland but brought Britain to the edge of civil war as Unionists in Ulster armed themselves to resist.

title: The Assassination of Abraham Lincoln
headline: PRESIDENT SHOT: Abraham Lincoln Assassinated at Ford's Theatre as Nation Celebrates War's End
summary: On April 14, 1865, five days after the Civil War ended, John Wilkes Booth shot President Abraham Lincoln at Ford's Theatre. Lincoln died the following morning, plunging a reuniting nation into grief.

title: The Battle of Thermopylae
headline: 300 HOLD THE PASS: King Leonidas and His Spartans Make Their Last Stand Against Persian Millions
summary: In 480 BC, King Leonidas of Sparta led 300 warriors and several thousand Greek allies to hold the narrow pass at Thermopylae against Xerxes' massive Persian army, buying Greece time to prepare its defense.

title: The Building of the Great Wall of China
headline: WALL ACROSS THE WORLD: Emperor Qin Orders 5,000-Mile Barrier to Shield China from Northern Invaders
summary: Beginning in 221 BC under Emperor Qin Shi Huang, China embarked on one of humanity's most ambitious construction projects: a defensive wall stretching thousands of miles across mountains and deserts.

title: The Eruption of Mount Vesuvius
headline: CITY BURIED ALIVE: Vesuvius Erupts, Entombing Pompeii Under Twenty Feet of Volcanic Ash
summary: On August 24, 79 AD, Mount Vesuvius erupted catastrophically, burying the Roman cities of Pompeii and Herculaneum under volcanic material and preserving a snapshot of daily life in the ancient world.
wiki: Eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 AD

title: The Library of Alexandria
headline: KNOWLEDGE OF THE WORLD: Alexandria's Great Library Collects Every Book Ever Written
summary: Founded in the 3rd century BC, the Library of Alexandria became the ancient world's greatest center of learning, housing hundreds of thousands of scrolls and attracting scholars from across the Mediterranean.

title: The Construction of the Panama Canal
headline: TWO OCEANS JOINED: After 27,000 Deaths, the Panama Canal Opens and Changes World Trade Forever
summary: Completed in 1914 after a decade of construction and thousands of worker deaths, the Panama Canal connected the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans, eliminating the 12,000-mile voyage around South America.

title: First Powered Flight at Kitty Hawk
headline: MAN FLIES: Wright Brothers Achieve 12-Second Powered Flight Over North Carolina Sand Dunes
summary: On December 17, 1903, Orville and Wilbur Wright achieved the first sustained, controlled, powered heavier-than-air flight near Kitty Hawk, North Carolina, launching the age of aviation.

title: The Sinking of the Lusitania
headline: LUXURY LINER TORPEDOED: 1,198 Dead as German U-Boat Sinks Lusitania Off Irish Coast
summary: On May 7, 1915, a German submarine torpedoed the RMS Lusitania, killing 1,198 passengers and crew. The sinking turned American public opinion against Germany and helped draw the U.S. into World War I.

title: The October Revolution
headline: BOLSHEVIKS SEIZE POWER: Lenin's Revolution Topples Government, Russia Exits World War
summary: On November 7, 1917, Bolshevik forces led by Vladimir Lenin stormed the Winter Palace in Petrograd, overthrowing the Provisional Government and establishing the world's first communist state.

title: Discovery of Tutankhamun's Tomb
headline: WONDERFUL THINGS: Howard Carter Opens Sealed Egyptian Tomb Untouched for 3,000 Years
summary: On November 26, 1922, archaeologist Howard Carter peered into the tomb of Pharaoh Tutankhamun and saw golden treasures that had lain undisturbed for over 3,000 years, sparking worldwide Egyptomania.

title: The Wall Street Crash of 1929
headline: MARKETS COLLAPSE: Black Tuesday Wipes Out Billions as Wall Street Plunges Into Chaos
summary: On October 29, 1929, the stock market crashed catastrophically on Black Tuesday, erasing billions in wealth and triggering the Great Depression that would devastate economies worldwide for a decade.

title: The Hindenburg Disaster
headline: OH THE HUMANITY: Giant Airship Hindenburg Explodes Over New Jersey, Ending the Age of the Zeppelin
summary: On May 6, 1937, the German airship Hindenburg burst into flames while landing at Lakehurst, New Jersey, killing 36 people and destroying public confidence in rigid airships forever.

title: The Battle of Stalingrad
headline: TURNING POINT: Soviet Forces Destroy German 6th Army at Stalingrad in Deadliest Battle in History
summary: From August 1942 to February 1943, the Battle of Stalingrad killed nearly two million people and ended in the destruction of Germany's 6th Army, marking the turning point of World War II in Europe.

title: The Atomic Bombing of Nagasaki
headline: SECOND BOMB DROPPED: Fat Man Devastates Nagasaki, Japan Surrenders Days Later
summary: On August 9, 1945, the United States dropped a plutonium bomb on Nagasaki, killing approximately 40,000 people instantly. Six days later, Japan announced its surrender, ending World War II.
wiki: Atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki

title: The Liberation of Paris
headline: PARIS IS FREE: Four Years of Nazi Occupation End as Allied Forces Enter the City of Light
summary: On August 25, 1944, Allied forces and the French Resistance liberated Paris after four years of German occupation, as crowds filled the Champs-Elysees in jubilant celebration.

title: The Founding of NATO
headline: WESTERN ALLIANCE: Twelve Nations Sign North Atlantic Treaty, Pledge Mutual Defense Against Soviet Threat
summary: On April 4, 1949, twelve nations signed the North Atlantic Treaty in Washington, D.C., creating a military alliance that would serve as the cornerstone of Western defense throughout the Cold War.

title: The Construction of the Berlin Wall
headline: CITY DIVIDED: East Germany Erects Wall Through Heart of Berlin Overnight
summary: On August 13, 1961, East German soldiers began building a barbed wire barrier through Berlin, eventually replaced by a concrete wall that would divide families and symbolize the Iron Curtain for 28 years.

title: The Bay of Pigs Invasion
headline: INVASION FAILS: CIA-Backed Cuban Exiles Crushed on Beach as Castro's Forces Counterattack
summary: On April 17, 1961, approximately 1,400 CIA-trained Cuban exiles landed at the Bay of Pigs to overthrow Fidel Castro. The invasion failed within three days, humiliating the Kennedy administration.

title: The Chernobyl Disaster
headline: REACTOR EXPLODES: World's Worst Nuclear Disaster Spreads Radiation Across Europe
summary: On April 26, 1986, Reactor No. 4 at the Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant in Ukraine exploded during a safety test, releasing 400 times more radiation than the Hiroshima bomb and contaminating vast areas of Europe.

title: The March on Washington
headline: I HAVE A DREAM: 250,000 March on Washington as King Delivers Greatest Speech of the Century
summary: On August 28, 1963, more than 250,000 people gathered at the Lincoln Memorial for the March on Washington, where Martin Luther King Jr. delivered his legendary 'I Have a Dream' speech.
wiki: March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom

title: The Selma to Montgomery Marches
headline: BLOODY SUNDAY TO VICTORY: Marchers Brave Tear Gas and Clubs to Win the Right to Vote
summary: In March 1965, three marches from Selma to Montgomery, Alabama highlighted the violent suppression of Black voting rights. The first march's Bloody Sunday images shocked the nation and led to the Voting Rights Act.

title: The Assassination of President Kennedy
headline: PRESIDENT KILLED: John F. Kennedy Shot Dead in Dallas Motorcade
summary: On November 22, 1963, President John F. Kennedy was assassinated while riding in an open motorcade through Dealey Plaza in Dallas, Texas, shocking the world and ending the era of Camelot.

title: The Woodstock Festival
headline: PEACE AND MUSIC: 400,000 Gather on New York Farm for Three Days of Music That Defined a Generation
summary: From August 15 to 18, 1969, the Woodstock Music and Art Fair drew 400,000 people to a dairy farm in Bethel, New York, becoming the defining cultural event of the 1960s counterculture movement.

title: The Fall of Saigon
headline: SAIGON FALLS: Last Americans Evacuate by Helicopter as North Vietnamese Tanks Enter the Capital
summary: On April 30, 1975, North Vietnamese forces captured Saigon, ending the Vietnam War. Iconic images of helicopters evacuating the last Americans from the embassy roof marked the end of two decades of U.S. involvement.

title: The Three Mile Island Accident
headline: NUCLEAR SCARE: Reactor Partially Melts Down in Pennsylvania, Sparking Nationwide Panic
summary: On March 28, 1979, a partial meltdown at the Three Mile Island nuclear plant in Pennsylvania became the worst nuclear accident in American history, transforming public attitudes toward nuclear energy.

title: The Camp David Accords
headline: PEACE IN THE MIDDLE EAST: Egypt and Israel Sign Historic Agreement After 13 Days at Camp David
summary: On September 17, 1978, Egyptian President Anwar Sadat and Israeli Prime Minister Menachem Begin signed the Camp David Accords, brokered by President Carter, ending 30 years of hostility between the two nations.

title: The End of Apartheid in South Africa
headline: APARTHEID FALLS: South Africa Holds First Free Elections as Mandela Becomes President
summary: On April 27, 1994, millions of South Africans of all races voted together for the first time in the country's history, electing Nelson Mandela president and ending decades of institutionalized racial segregation.

title: The Reunification of Germany
headline: ONE GERMANY: East and West Officially Reunite After 45 Years of Cold War Division
summary: On October 3, 1990, East and West Germany officially reunified, ending 45 years of division. The Berlin Wall had fallen less than a year earlier, and now the two halves of Germany became one nation again.

title: The Birth of the Internet
headline: CONNECTED: ARPANET Sends First Message, Laying the Foundation for a Network That Will Change Everything
summary: On October 29, 1969, the first message was sent over ARPANET from UCLA to Stanford. The system crashed after two letters, but this humble beginning would evolve into the internet that connects billions today.

title: The Discovery of DNA's Double Helix
headline: SECRET OF LIFE: Watson and Crick Reveal the Structure of DNA in Cambridge Pub Announcement
summary: On February 28, 1953, James Watson and Francis Crick determined the double-helix structure of DNA, unlocking the molecular basis of heredity and launching the era of molecular biology.

title: The First Successful Organ Transplant
headline: MEDICAL MIRACLE: Surgeon Successfully Transplants Kidney Between Identical Twins
summary: On December 23, 1954, Dr. Joseph Murray performed the first successful organ transplant at Peter Bent Brigham Hospital in Boston, transplanting a kidney between identical twins and opening a new era in medicine.

title: Gutenberg's Printing Press
headline: KNOWLEDGE UNLEASHED: Gutenberg's Invention Allows Books to Be Printed by the Thousand
summary: Around 1440, Johannes Gutenberg developed movable-type printing in Mainz, Germany. His invention democratized knowledge, fueled the Renaissance and Reformation, and remains one of humanity's most transformative innovations.

title: Columbus Reaches the Americas
headline: NEW WORLD FOUND: Columbus Lands on Caribbean Island After 36 Days at Sea
summary: On October 12, 1492, Christopher Columbus and his crew made landfall in the Bahamas, initiating sustained European contact with the Americas and setting in motion centuries of profound cultural and ecological exchange.

title: The Signing of Magna Carta
headline: KING BOWS TO LAW: English Barons Force King John to Seal Charter Limiting Royal Power
summary: On June 15, 1215, English barons forced King John to seal Magna Carta at Runnymede, establishing the principle that even the king was subject to law and planting the seeds of constitutional government.

title: The Black Death Reaches Europe
headline: PLAGUE SWEEPS CONTINENT: Black Death Kills One-Third of Europe's Population
summary: Between 1347 and 1353, the Black Death killed an estimated 25 to 50 million Europeans, roughly one-third of the continent's population, reshaping medieval society, labor markets, and religious institutions.

title: The First Crusade
headline: DEUS VULT: Pope Urban II Calls Christendom to Arms, Launching Two Centuries of Holy Wars
summary: On November 27, 1095, Pope Urban II called on Christian Europe to reclaim Jerusalem from Muslim control. The First Crusade succeeded in capturing Jerusalem in 1099, beginning nearly 200 years of religious warfare.

title: The Steam Engine Revolution
headline: POWER UNLEASHED: Watt's Improved Steam Engine Launches the Industrial Revolution
summary: James Watt's improved steam engine, patented in 1769, transformed manufacturing, mining, and transportation, powering the Industrial Revolution and fundamentally changing how humanity produces goods.

title: Lindbergh's Transatlantic Flight
headline: LONE EAGLE LANDS IN PARIS: Lindbergh Completes First Solo Nonstop Flight Across the Atlantic
summary: On May 21, 1927, Charles Lindbergh landed the Spirit of St. Louis at Le Bourget Field in Paris after 33.5 hours of solo flight from New York, completing the first nonstop transatlantic airplane flight.

title: Women Win the Right to Vote
headline: VICTORY AT LAST: 19th Amendment Ratified, Giving 26 Million American Women the Right to Vote
summary: On August 18, 1920, Tennessee became the 36th state to ratify the 19th Amendment, granting women the right to vote after 72 years of organized activism in the American suffrage movement.
wiki: Nineteenth Amendment to the United States Constitution

title: The Spanish Civil War
headline: SPAIN TORN APART: Military Uprising Splits Nation as Europe Watches a Rehearsal for World War
summary: From 1936 to 1939, the Spanish Civil War pitted Republican loyalists against Nationalist rebels led by General Francisco Franco. The conflict served as a proving ground for the weapons and tactics of World War II.

title: The Dust Bowl
headline: BLACK BLIZZARDS: Massive Dust Storms Bury Farms Across the Great Plains
summary: Throughout the 1930s, severe drought and decades of poor farming practices created devastating dust storms across the American Great Plains, displacing hundreds of thousands of families during the Great Depression.

title: The Battle of Britain
headline: THEIR FINEST HOUR: RAF Pilots Hold Off Luftwaffe in the Skies Over England
summary: From July to October 1940, the Royal Air Force defended Britain against massive German air attacks. The RAF's victory in the Battle of Britain was the first major defeat of Hitler's military forces.

title: The Yalta Conference
headline: BIG THREE DIVIDE THE WORLD: Roosevelt, Churchill, and Stalin Reshape Postwar Europe
summary: In February 1945, Roosevelt, Churchill, and Stalin met at Yalta in Crimea to plan the final defeat of Nazi Germany and negotiate the postwar order, decisions that would shape the Cold War for decades.

title: The Tokyo War Crimes Tribunal
headline: JUSTICE IN THE PACIFIC: International Court Tries Japanese Leaders for War Crimes
summary: From 1946 to 1948, the International Military Tribunal for the Far East tried 28 Japanese military and political leaders for war crimes, crimes against peace, and crimes against humanity.
wiki: International Military Tribunal for the Far East

title: Indian Independence and Partition
headline: FREEDOM AT MIDNIGHT: India Wins Independence but Partition Triggers History's Largest Migration
summary: On August 15, 1947, India gained independence from British rule. The simultaneous partition into India and Pakistan triggered massive population transfers and communal violence that killed up to two million people.

title: The Creation of the State of Israel
headline: NEW NATION BORN: David Ben-Gurion Declares Israeli Independence as Five Arab Nations Prepare for War
summary: On May 14, 1948, David Ben-Gurion proclaimed the establishment of the State of Israel, fulfilling decades of Zionist aspiration. Within hours, neighboring Arab states invaded, beginning the 1948 Arab-Israeli War.

title: The Berlin Airlift
headline: CANDY BOMBERS: Western Allies Fly 2.3 Million Tons of Supplies Into Blockaded Berlin
summary: From June 1948 to May 1949, the Western Allies airlifted food, fuel, and supplies to the people of West Berlin after the Soviet Union blockaded all ground routes into the city.

title: The Launch of Sputnik
headline: RED MOON RISING: Soviet Union Launches First Artificial Satellite, Shocking the World
summary: On October 4, 1957, the Soviet Union launched Sputnik 1, the first artificial satellite to orbit Earth. Its steady beeping signal from space terrified Americans and ignited the Space Race.

title: Yuri Gagarin Orbits the Earth
headline: MAN IN SPACE: Soviet Cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin Becomes First Human to Orbit the Earth
summary: On April 12, 1961, Soviet cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin completed a single orbit of Earth aboard Vostok 1, becoming the first human being in space and scoring a major victory in the Space Race.

title: The Challenger Disaster
headline: TRAGEDY IN THE SKY: Space Shuttle Challenger Breaks Apart 73 Seconds After Launch
summary: On January 28, 1986, the Space Shuttle Challenger broke apart 73 seconds after launch, killing all seven crew members including teacher Christa McAuliffe, as millions of schoolchildren watched on live television.

title: Valentina Tereshkova: First Woman in Space
headline: SHE ORBITS ALONE: Soviet Cosmonaut Valentina Tereshkova Becomes First Woman in Space
summary: On June 16, 1963, Valentina Tereshkova launched aboard Vostok 6 and orbited the Earth 48 times over three days, becoming the first woman in space — a record that would stand for 19 years.

title: The Defeat of the Spanish Armada
headline: ARMADA DESTROYED: England's Navy and Storms Shatter Spain's Invasion Fleet
summary: In August 1588, England's smaller but more maneuverable navy, aided by fierce storms, defeated the mighty Spanish Armada, securing English naval dominance and Protestant independence from Catholic Spain.

title: The Gunpowder Plot
headline: PARLIAMENT SAVED: Guy Fawkes Caught With 36 Barrels of Gunpowder Beneath House of Lords
summary: On November 5, 1605, Guy Fawkes was discovered guarding 36 barrels of gunpowder beneath the House of Lords, foiling a Catholic conspiracy to assassinate King James I and blow up Parliament.

title: The Great Fire of London
headline: LONDON ABLAZE: Four-Day Fire Destroys 13,200 Houses and 87 Churches
summary: The Great Fire of London raged from September 2 to 6, 1666, destroying the medieval city within the old Roman wall. The fire consumed 13,200 houses and 87 churches but led to London's modern rebuilding.

title: The Treaty of Westphalia
headline: PEACE AFTER THIRTY YEARS: European Powers Sign Treaties That Create Modern Nation-State System
summary: The Peace of Westphalia in 1648 ended the devastating Thirty Years' War and established the principles of national sovereignty and non-interference that form the foundation of modern international relations.

title: The Abolition of Serfdom in Russia
headline: SERFS FREED: Tsar Alexander II Emancipates 23 Million Russian Peasants
summary: On March 3, 1861, Tsar Alexander II signed the Emancipation Reform, freeing approximately 23 million serfs from bondage in the Russian Empire, the largest emancipation in European history.

title: The Opening of Ellis Island
headline: GATEWAY TO AMERICA: Ellis Island Opens as 12 Million Immigrants Begin Journey to New Lives
summary: On January 1, 1892, Ellis Island opened as the United States' busiest immigration station. Over the next 62 years, more than 12 million immigrants would pass through its halls seeking a new life in America.

title: The Boxer Rebellion
headline: SIEGE OF THE LEGATIONS: Eight-Nation Alliance Marches on Beijing as Boxer Uprising Threatens Foreigners
summary: In 1900, the Boxer Rebellion saw Chinese martial artists attack foreign nationals and Chinese Christians, leading to a 55-day siege of foreign legations in Beijing and an eight-nation military intervention.

title: The Russo-Japanese War
headline: JAPAN STUNS THE WORLD: First Asian Power to Defeat a European Nation in Modern War
summary: The Russo-Japanese War of 1904-1905 stunned the world when Japan decisively defeated Russia, marking the first time an Asian power defeated a European one in modern warfare and reshaping global power dynamics.

title: The Invention of Radio
headline: VOICES THROUGH AIR: Marconi Sends First Wireless Signal Across the Atlantic
summary: On December 12, 1901, Guglielmo Marconi received the first transatlantic wireless signal in Newfoundland, proving radio waves could travel beyond the horizon and launching the age of broadcast communication.

title: The Treaty of Tordesillas
headline: WORLD DIVIDED: Spain and Portugal Split the Globe Between Them With a Single Line
summary: On June 7, 1494, Spain and Portugal signed the Treaty of Tordesillas, drawing an imaginary line through the Atlantic Ocean that divided the entire non-Christian world between the two empires.

title: Copernicus Publishes the Heliocentric Theory
headline: EARTH IS NOT THE CENTER: Copernicus Reveals the Sun Sits at the Heart of the Solar System
summary: In 1543, Nicolaus Copernicus published De revolutionibus orbium coelestium, proposing that the Earth and planets revolve around the Sun, overturning 1,400 years of geocentric astronomy.

title: The Invention of Dynamite
headline: CONTROLLED DESTRUCTION: Alfred Nobel Patents Dynamite, Making Mining and Construction Safer
summary: In 1867, Alfred Nobel patented dynamite, a safer way to harness the explosive power of nitroglycerin. The invention revolutionized construction and mining but also transformed warfare, leading Nobel to fund his famous Peace Prize.

title: Completion of the Transcontinental Railroad
headline: GOLDEN SPIKE: East Meets West as Transcontinental Railroad Joins at Promontory Summit
summary: On May 10, 1869, a golden spike was driven at Promontory Summit, Utah, completing the first transcontinental railroad and reducing cross-country travel from six months to six days.

title: The Discovery of X-Rays
headline: SEEING THROUGH FLESH: Rontgen Discovers Mysterious Rays That Reveal the Skeleton Inside the Body
summary: On November 8, 1895, Wilhelm Rontgen accidentally discovered X-rays while experimenting with cathode rays, producing the first medical image of his wife's hand — and revolutionizing medicine forever.

title: Florence Nightingale in Crimea
headline: LADY WITH THE LAMP: Nightingale's Reforms Cut Death Rates and Launch Modern Nursing
summary: In 1854, Florence Nightingale arrived at Scutari military hospital in Crimea and transformed it from a death trap into a model of sanitary care, reducing the death rate from 42 percent to 2 percent.

title: The End of the Cold War
headline: COLD WAR OVER: Bush and Gorbachev Declare End to 45 Years of Superpower Confrontation
summary: On December 3, 1989, President George H.W. Bush and Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev declared the Cold War over at a summit in Malta, ending 45 years of nuclear standoff between the superpowers.

title: The Tiananmen Square Protests
headline: TANK MAN: One Protester Stands Before a Column of Tanks in Beijing
summary: In June 1989, the Chinese government violently suppressed pro-democracy protests in Tiananmen Square, killing hundreds or thousands of civilians. The iconic image of a lone man blocking a tank column became a global symbol of resistance.

title: The Rwandan Genocide
headline: 100 DAYS OF HORROR: 800,000 Murdered in Rwanda as the World Looks Away
summary: From April to July 1994, Hutu extremists in Rwanda systematically murdered approximately 800,000 Tutsi and moderate Hutu people in approximately 100 days while the international community failed to intervene.

title: The Dayton Peace Agreement
headline: PEACE IN BOSNIA: Warring Factions Sign Agreement Ending Europe's Bloodiest Conflict Since 1945
summary: On November 21, 1995, the Dayton Peace Agreement ended the Bosnian War, which had killed over 100,000 people. The accord, brokered at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, created the modern state of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

title: The Kyoto Protocol
headline: CLIMATE PACT: 192 Nations Agree to Cut Greenhouse Gas Emissions for the First Time
summary: On December 11, 1997, delegates from 192 nations adopted the Kyoto Protocol, the first international treaty to set binding targets for reducing greenhouse gas emissions and combating climate change.

title: The International Space Station
headline: HOME IN SPACE: Former Cold War Rivals Build Permanent Laboratory Orbiting 250 Miles Above Earth
summary: Launched in 1998, the International Space Station became the largest structure ever built in space, a symbol of international cooperation where astronauts from 19 countries have lived and worked together.

title: Mapping the Human Genome
headline: CODE OF LIFE CRACKED: Scientists Complete Map of All 3 Billion Letters in Human DNA
summary: On April 14, 2003, the Human Genome Project announced the complete mapping of the human genome's 3 billion base pairs, opening a new era of personalized medicine and genetic understanding.

title: The 2004 Indian Ocean Tsunami
headline: WAVE OF DESTRUCTION: Massive Tsunami Kills 230,000 Across 14 Countries
summary: On December 26, 2004, a magnitude 9.1 earthquake off Sumatra triggered a tsunami that killed approximately 230,000 people across 14 countries, prompting the largest international relief effort in history.

title: The Arab Spring
headline: REVOLUTION SPREADS: Street Protests Topple Governments Across the Middle East
summary: Beginning in December 2010, a wave of pro-democracy protests swept across the Arab world, toppling long-standing dictators in Tunisia, Egypt, and Libya while triggering civil wars in Syria and Yemen.

title: The Fukushima Nuclear Disaster
headline: TRIPLE MELTDOWN: Earthquake and Tsunami Cause Worst Nuclear Disaster Since Chernobyl
summary: On March 11, 2011, a magnitude 9.0 earthquake and tsunami triggered three nuclear meltdowns at the Fukushima Daiichi power plant in Japan, causing the worst nuclear accident since Chernobyl.

title: Curiosity Rover Lands on Mars
headline: TOUCHDOWN ON MARS: NASA's Curiosity Rover Survives Seven Minutes of Terror to Land on Red Planet
summary: On August 6, 2012, NASA's Curiosity rover successfully landed on Mars using an unprecedented sky-crane system, beginning a mission to determine whether the Red Planet ever supported microbial life.

title: The West African Ebola Outbreak
headline: EBOLA CRISIS: Deadliest Outbreak in History Kills 11,000 Across West Africa
summary: From 2013 to 2016, the worst Ebola epidemic in history swept through Guinea, Liberia, and Sierra Leone, killing over 11,000 people and overwhelming health systems across West Africa.

title: The Detection of Gravitational Waves
headline: EINSTEIN WAS RIGHT: Scientists Detect Ripples in Spacetime from Colliding Black Holes
summary: On September 14, 2015, the LIGO observatory detected gravitational waves from two merging black holes 1.3 billion light-years away, confirming Einstein's century-old prediction and opening a new window on the universe.

title: The Fall of the Aztec Empire
headline: TENOCHTITLAN FALLS: Cortes and Native Allies Conquer the Aztec Capital After 80-Day Siege
summary: On August 13, 1521, Spanish conquistador Hernan Cortes and his indigenous allies captured Tenochtitlan after an 80-day siege, ending the Aztec Empire and beginning Spanish colonial rule in Mexico.

title: The Haitian Slave Rebellion
headline: SLAVES RISE UP: Massive Rebellion in Saint-Domingue Shakes the Foundations of Colonial Slavery
summary: On August 22, 1791, enslaved people in the French colony of Saint-Domingue launched the largest slave revolt in the Americas, beginning a 13-year revolution that would create the independent nation of Haiti.

title: The Invention of the Telegraph
headline: WHAT HATH GOD WROUGHT: Morse Sends First Telegraphic Message from Washington to Baltimore
summary: On May 24, 1844, Samuel Morse sent the message 'What hath God wrought' from Washington to Baltimore, demonstrating the electric telegraph and ushering in the age of instant long-distance communication.

title: The Berlin Conference and the Scramble for Africa
headline: CONTINENT CARVED UP: European Powers Divide Africa Among Themselves Without African Input
summary: From November 1884 to February 1885, European powers met in Berlin to establish rules for the colonization of Africa, drawing borders that ignored ethnic and cultural boundaries and reshaping the continent.

title: The Battle of Waterloo
headline: NAPOLEON DEFEATED: Wellington and Blucher Crush the Emperor at Waterloo, Ending 23 Years of War
summary: On June 18, 1815, the Duke of Wellington and Prussian forces defeated Napoleon Bonaparte at Waterloo in Belgium, ending the Napoleonic Wars and reshaping the map of Europe.

title: The Treaty of Nanking
headline: UNEQUAL TREATY: China Forced to Cede Hong Kong and Open Five Ports to British Trade
summary: On August 29, 1842, China signed the Treaty of Nanking ending the First Opium War, ceding Hong Kong to Britain and opening five treaty ports, beginning a century of unequal treaties with Western powers.

title: The September 11 Attacks
headline: AMERICA UNDER ATTACK: Hijacked Planes Strike World Trade Center and Pentagon
summary: On September 11, 2001, terrorists hijacked four commercial airliners, crashing two into the World Trade Center towers and one into the Pentagon, killing 2,977 people in the deadliest terrorist attack in history.

title: The Legacy of Apollo
headline: BEYOND THE MOON: How Apollo Reshaped Science, Technology, and What Humanity Believes Is Possible
summary: The Apollo program did not just put men on the Moon. It created technologies, inspired generations, and proved that humanity could achieve the impossible when united behind a common goal.

title: The Unification of Italy
headline: ITALIA UNITA: Garibaldi and Cavour Forge One Nation from a Patchwork of Kingdoms
summary: Between 1859 and 1871, the Italian unification movement brought together dozens of separate states and kingdoms into a single nation, ending centuries of foreign domination and division.

title: The Spanish Inquisition
headline: NOBODY EXPECTS IT: Ferdinand and Isabella Establish the Spanish Inquisition to Enforce Religious Orthodoxy
summary: Established in 1478, the Spanish Inquisition became one of history's most feared institutions, interrogating and punishing suspected heretics for over 350 years and expelling Jews and Muslims from Spain.

title: The Invention of the Magnetic Compass
headline: FINDING TRUE NORTH: Chinese Invention Revolutionizes Navigation and Opens the World to Exploration
summary: Developed in China during the 11th century, the magnetic compass revolutionized maritime navigation, enabling the great voyages of exploration that connected the continents and reshaped human civilization.

title: The Boston Massacre
headline: BLOOD ON THE SNOW: British Soldiers Fire Into Crowd of Colonists, Killing Five
summary: On March 5, 1770, British soldiers fired into a crowd of American colonists in Boston, killing five men. The incident was used as powerful propaganda that helped build support for American independence.

title: The Mongol Siege of Baghdad
headline: CITY OF WISDOM DESTROYED: Mongol Horde Sacks Baghdad, Ending the Islamic Golden Age
summary: In February 1258, Mongol forces under Hulagu Khan sacked Baghdad, destroying the House of Wisdom and killing an estimated 200,000 to one million people, ending five centuries of Abbasid caliphate rule.

title: The Defenestration of Prague
headline: THROWN FROM THE WINDOW: Prague Incident Sparks Thirty Years of War Across Europe
summary: On May 23, 1618, Protestant nobles threw two Catholic imperial governors out of a window in Prague Castle, triggering the Thirty Years War that would kill eight million people across Europe.

title: The Louisiana Purchase Negotiations
headline: CONTINENT FOR SALE: Napoleon Offers to Sell 828,000 Square Miles for Just $15 Million
summary: In April 1803, Napoleon unexpectedly offered to sell the entire Louisiana Territory to the United States, doubling the nation's size overnight for roughly four cents per acre.

title: Alexander Graham Bell and the Telephone
headline: MR. WATSON, COME HERE: Bell Transmits First Intelligible Speech by Wire
summary: On March 10, 1876, Alexander Graham Bell spoke the first words ever transmitted by telephone to his assistant Thomas Watson, launching a communications revolution that would connect the world.

title: The Great Kanto Earthquake
headline: TOKYO IN RUINS: Massive Earthquake and Firestorm Kill 140,000 in Japan's Worst Natural Disaster
summary: On September 1, 1923, a magnitude 7.9 earthquake struck the Kanto region of Japan, triggering firestorms that destroyed Tokyo and Yokohama, killing approximately 140,000 people.

title: Nasser Nationalizes the Suez Canal
headline: CANAL SEIZED: Egypt's Nasser Takes Control of Suez, Defying Britain and France
summary: On July 26, 1956, Egyptian President Gamal Abdel Nasser nationalized the Suez Canal, provoking an international crisis that ended European colonial dominance in the Middle East.

title: Nelson Mandela's Inauguration
headline: RAINBOW NATION: Mandela Sworn In as South Africa's First Black President Before 100,000 Jubilant Citizens
summary: On May 10, 1994, Nelson Mandela was inaugurated as South Africa's first Black president in Pretoria, marking the definitive end of apartheid before a crowd of 100,000 and dignitaries from 140 countries.

title: The First Television Broadcast
headline: PICTURES THROUGH THE AIR: BBC Launches World's First Regular Television Service
summary: On November 2, 1936, the BBC launched the world's first regular high-definition television service from Alexandra Palace in London, beginning a medium that would transform culture, politics, and daily life.
